Q1: Butyraldehyde exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive toxicity (CMR), environmental impact (ENV), and organ and systemic toxicity (OGN) according to the Globally Harmonized System. It also shows potential dermal and eye hazards (SKN) based on an expanded perspective beyond GHS, while demonstrating low to moderate hazards for endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation (IHL), and oral exposure (ORL).
Q2: Butyraldehyde is not currently identified on any specific "Lists of Concern." However, it is included in the EPA's "Substances Added to Food" inventory, indicating it is generally considered of low hazard, particularly when used under regulated conditions as a food additive or color additive.
Q3: Butyraldehyde is extensively characterized, with 33,000 literature references, far exceeding the median for petrochemicals in our database. Its clearly defined molecular formula (C4H8O), "Small Molecule" substance class, and absence of data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard classifications further confirm its well-understood nature.
